result_text:
`push_lossy` on a zero-capacity `Outbox` now counts one drop and returns without queuing, so the queue stays empty and `pop()` after `close()` returns None. `cargo check -p shep-channel` passes. It prints 4 dead-code warnings, and I didn't check whether they were there before my edit. I didn't run any tests.

The change is in `crates/shep-channel/src/outbox.rs`. The zero-capacity check sits after the closed check, so a push after `close()` is still ignored and not counted. Capacities of one or more take the same path as before. I also added a sentence to the `push_lossy` doc comment about the zero case.

Separate from this task, `push_blocking` on a zero-capacity outbox waits for room that never comes, so it blocks until the outbox closes. I left it alone since you only asked about `push_lossy`.

Next: run `cargo test -p shep-channel --lib` to check the existing outbox tests still pass.
